Today's TL;DRRegimeMIXED
Markets are caught between a soft U.S. jobs surprise that fuels rate-cut expectations and a tech/AI rebound that pushes indices to records, while escalating geopolitical risks (Iran, trade wars, Fed politicization) and commodity supply fears keep volatility high. The bull case rests on AI monetization, institutional cash deployment, and crypto adoption; the bear case warns of debt indigestion, Fed splits, and supply-chain disruptions.

BernsteinBofACitiDeutsche BankGoldman SachsJ.P. MorganMorgan StanleyNomuraUBS
AI infrastructure capex boomAI基础设施资本支出繁荣
×11 · 43 steps
AI infrastructure spending is accelerating, with Big Tech capex expected to grow ~100% YoY to $730bn in 2026 and surpass $1tn by 2028, driving strong profit growth for AI infrastructure stocks and supporting AI ecosystems globally, including in China. AWS demand visibility into 2028 with a $496bn backlog and a path to $1tn annual revenue; management raised 2026 capex to ~$220bn and sees elevated investment continuing through 2027-2028. Cloud AI capex drives demand for optical components, semiconductor test equipment, and natural gas power generation, with Goldman Sachs noting a $100bn Kentucky data center campus requiring ~400 mmcf/d of gas throughput.

China domestic demand weakness vs easing中国内需疲弱与宽松预期
×7 · 25 steps
China's domestic demand is weakening across multiple sectors: official manufacturing PMI fell sharply in July to 49.8, property sales worsened to -14.6% ytd in July, and secondary home prices fell 0.5% m/m in July (down 9.6% y/y). The July Politburo meeting strengthened easing rhetoric and emphasized faster implementation of planned measures, with ~RMB1.8tn in unused bond quota and a new RMB800bn policy-based financial instrument, but Goldman expects no rate cuts in 2026. China economic activity softened in July, with steel demand and production declining, manufacturing PMI contracting, and property transactions weak. Property activity indicators are down 60-80% from 2020-21 peaks, fiscal tightening contributed nearly half of the Q1-to-Q2 GDP slowdown.

Memory and semiconductor pricing upcycle存储与半导体涨价周期
×7 · 26 steps
Memory demand from AI/server is significantly outstripping supply, with the gap widening into 2028; this is driving pricing increases (HBM pricing up 87% yoy, NAND pricing up 23% in June) and elevated margins (DRAM ~80%, NAND ~60%). NAND demand for AI inference/agentic applications is increasing significantly, expected to exceed supply through CY27. Memory cost hikes pressure non-memory component margins across supply chain, leading to cost reduction pressure on non-memory components. Storage undersupply driving pricing power: SanDisk has locked in over 50% of FY27-28 bit production at ~80% gross margins, while Western Digital reports nearline HDD sold out into CY28 with price/exabyte growing 18% Y/Y. DRAM undersupply set to persist through at least Q2 2028, with DDR ASPs rising from $0.40/Gb in 2025 to $2.24/Gb in 2027 and HBM ASPs to $3.13/Gb.
17 extracted · 6 firms

Broad consensus on memory supply-demand tightness driving a pricing upcycle, with dissent focusing on downstream margin pressure and demand elasticity.市场普遍认同存储供需偏紧推动涨价周期，分歧集中于下游利润率压力和需求弹性。

AI spillover into factory automationAI溢出至工厂自动化
×6 · 23 steps
AI and datacenter demand remains robust, driving growth in semiconductor equipment and components, and spilling over into adjacent industries such as factory automation and semi capital equipment. Japan's machine tool orders from China grew 49.1% YoY in June (broad-based), with overall orders accelerating to 45.5% YoY (vs 37.3% in May); AC servo and CNC sales each grew 25% YoY in Q2, and industrial robot production grew 28.1% YoY in June, forming a 'twin peaks' pattern. WFE market is in an upcycle driven by AI, with rising litho intensity as DRAM and advanced logic adoption of EUV/HNA increases; Tokyo Electron improved CY27 WFE outlook to $190bn and expects >50% growth in coaters/etchers.

AI-Driven Component Supply TightnessAI驱动的元件供应紧张
×5 · 22 steps
AI demand for servers, MLCCs, and CCLs is causing supply tightness and pricing power across multiple high-end electronic component markets, with MLCC export prices up +4% mom, CCL pricing hikes expected in 2H26, and LTA commitments reaching 60-70% of memory capacity. MLCC utilization rates exceeding 90% and book-to-bill rising to 2.2x. Yageo is well positioned to benefit and may see price hikes for midrange as suppliers shift capacity to high-end. Japanese MLCC supply-demand tightness enables price hikes and contract renegotiations, with some customers beginning to accept price increases to secure volumes.

US-China trade and tech tensions美中贸易与科技紧张局势
×5 · 14 steps
Trade and technology tensions between the US and China are escalating, with new US tariffs on polysilicon, bans on foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots, and potential import bans on Chinese-manufactured optical components for AI data centers. The US FCC banned foreign-made robots on 28 July 2026, impacting Chinese makers and pushing component production to Thailand, Mexico, and the US. US import ban on Chinese optical components would affect Chinese module makers (over 50% of high-speed modules to US CSPs) and potentially benefit non-Chinese manufacturers. The EU is mulling countervailing tariffs on Chinese PHEVs. However, US-China also saw constructive development on a $30bn tariff reduction package.

Pricing power and cost pass-through variability across sectors定价能力与成本传导的行业差异
×6 · 24 steps
Companies differ in ability to pass on cost increases: Renesas implemented price hikes from July 1 and L'Oréal achieved volume and value growth, while Murata has only partially considered pricing adjustments due to cost increases in energy, precious metals, and labor. Companies across sectors are demonstrating pricing power by passing through higher costs, seen in Monster Beverage (planned US pricing increase), LG Uplus (higher AIDC pricing), GlobalFoundries (pricing actions), and Klaviyo (carrier-fee pass-through). Supply-demand tightness in AI hardware is enabling price increases and margin expansion: ON Semi raised prices and improved utilization from 77% to 83%, Wistron renegotiated terms and expects margin improvement.

China fiscal policy fine-tuning中国财政政策微调
×4 · 16 steps
Chinese policymakers are increasing fiscal and monetary support through local government bond issuance and consumption stimulus, but implementation lags and structural issues persist. Weak July manufacturing PMIs (output PMI at 49.9, new orders at 48.5) increase pressure on Beijing to implement faster fiscal spending and bond deployment. July Politburo meeting emphasized policy fine-tuning rather than a pivot, with an Rmb2tn fiscal impulse available for 2H26 and potential additional easing if growth disappoints in July-August.

×7 · 26 steps
The Middle East conflict is causing naphtha feedstock shortages and higher oil prices that weigh on chemical margins, sharply reducing China's exports to the Middle East by 21.5% yoy while raising energy import prices, and tightening financial conditions by an equivalent of 47bp rate hike. Re-escalation between US and Iran, Houthi threats in Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, and halted LNG transit via Strait of Hormuz drove Brent crude +23.6% in July (best-performing major asset). China reduced oil imports by 30.3% y/y in Q2 and drew SPR down by 320mb in Q2, making China the major shock absorber for global oil markets.

AI positioning unwindAI板块仓位去杠杆
×3 · 12 steps
The AI sector correction in July 2026 was driven by an intense positioning unwind after a momentum rally, with hedge funds and retail leverage moderating. Gross leverage reversed half its yearly increase, marking the second-largest 2-day long selling in a decade. AxJ Tech later recovered almost half its July losses. Korea leveraged ETF AUM fell from peak $53bn to $24bn; margin loans declined only 14% from peak while deposits fell 22%, pushing margin-loan-to-deposit ratio from 17% to 26%.

ABF substrate undersupply tighteningABF基板供应紧缺收紧
×2 · 8 steps
ABF substrate supply-demand is tightening: Morgan Stanley's model points to 25% undersupply by 2030. Ajinomoto raised ABF film prices 30% for Q3 2026, implying ~5.9% and ~3.6% pass-through to CPU and AI substrate pricing. The market has shifted structurally from PC-dominated (70% in 2015) to server/AI-dominated (60% in 2025, >80% by 2030). Ajinomoto's ABF materials revenue growth accelerated to 54% YoY with business profit margin expanding 470bps to 57.7%.

US Jobs Shock: July Payrolls Unexpectedly Contract
Nonfarm payrolls unexpectedly fell by 23,000 in July, the first monthly contraction of the cycle, against a consensus expectation of +83,000. The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1% (US Insider) or held at 4.2% (CNBC/Dow Jones), while labor force participation fell and prior months were revised lower. Economists warn that falling long-term unemployment reflects workers leaving the labor force, not hiring. This sharp downside surprise is likely to reignite Fed rate-cut bets and weigh on risk assets.

This has driven oil prices higher, boosted safe-haven gold, and created volatility across energy equities, tanker rates, and defensive currencies.
